## Marketing Performance Snapshot

Email was the strongest channel in this dataset: it generated the highest engagement and the best efficiency, especially in the week of **2026-01-19**. For dashboarding, the clearest view is a mix of a trend chart and an efficiency chart.

## Weekly Metrics and Best-Performing Week

| Week | Email Opens | Email Clicks | CTR | Ad Spend | Leads | Cost per Lead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-01-05 | 4,200 | 310 | 7.38% | 1,800 | 74 | 24.32 |
| 2026-01-12 | 3,900 | 295 | 7.56% | 1,700 | 69 | 24.64 |
| 2026-01-19 | 5,100 | 410 | 8.04% | 2,200 | 88 | 25.00 |
| 2026-01-26 | 4,800 | 380 | 7.92% | 2,100 | 81 | 25.93 |

CTR formula: **Email Clicks ÷ Email Opens × 100**
Cost per lead formula: **Ad Spend ÷ Leads**

## Recommended Dashboard Charts

### 1) Multi-series line chart
Best for showing week-over-week movement in:
- Email Opens
- Email Clicks
- Leads

Why it works:
- Makes trends and spikes easy to spot
- Good for comparing volume changes over time
- Helps identify whether engagement and lead volume rise together

### 2) Combo chart with bars and line
Best for showing efficiency:
- Bars: Ad Spend and Leads
- Line: Cost per Lead

Why it works:
- Shows whether higher spend is producing proportionally more leads
- Makes efficiency changes obvious
- Good executive-level KPI view

## Plain-Language Insights

- **2026-01-19 was the best week overall.** It had the most opens, clicks, and leads, and also the highest CTR at **8.04%**.
- **Engagement improved as volume increased.** When opens rose, clicks also rose, which suggests the email content and targeting were working well.
- **Efficiency was slightly worse in the last week.** Cost per lead climbed to **25.93**, even though leads stayed strong, so spend was becoming less efficient.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Build line chart](https://www.google.com/search?q=dashboard+line+chart+email+opens+clicks+leads)
Action: [Button: Build combo chart](https://www.google.com/search?q=dashboard+combo+chart+ad+spend+leads+cost+per+lead)

## Sources

- Formula reference for CTR and CPL: https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/cost-per-lead.asp
- Chart selection guidance: https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/data-visualization
